raw_response:
The silver step derives txn_date from ingest_ts, but the date should come from txn_ts. The 2026-01-16 refactor (DE-398) is the likely cause. Ingest runs at 02:00 the day after the transaction, so every row has txn_date one day later than the date of txn_ts. The alert counts 4630 mismatches, which equals the total number of POSTED rows, so all rows are off by one day.

The date of txn_ts is the clear intended semantics, and the monitor checks exactly that. The fix is to set txn_date to CAST(txn_ts AS DATE).

Check on the data: txn_ts is already TIMESTAMP, and the sample rows show txn_ts on the day before ingest. The 4630 mismatches match the POSTED count exactly, so no rows would remain inconsistent after the fix.

The gold tables are built from silver_transactions, so they are corrected automatically once silver is rebuilt, with no override needed. I don't see duplicate txn_ids (distinct = rows), so no dedup is needed. Excluding REVERSED rows is existing behavior, so I leave it unchanged.

{"diagnosis": "The DE-398 refactor derives txn_date from ingest_ts (which is 02:00 the next day) instead of txn_ts, so every POSTED row (4630) has txn_date shifted by one day. Deriving txn_date from txn_ts fixes silver and, through it, all gold tables.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
